\n

Companies in Amberford and Ostara account for just over half the approved lending by value. Purchases include cutting machines, temperature-controlled storage and packing lines. import urllib.parse
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser
from typing import List, Dict

class FetchError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: int):
        self.status = status
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status}")

def extract(fetch, listing_url: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Extract all press releases from the listing page.
    Returns list of dicts with keys: url, title, date, author, body.
    Newest first.
    """
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    
    table = soup.find("table", class_="bok-table")
    if not table:
        return []
    
    rows = table.find_all("tr", recursive=False)
    records = []
    
    for row in rows:
        # Find date cell and title <a>
        date_cell = row.find(class_="date")
        title_a = row.find("a", href=True)
        if not date_cell or not title_a:
            continue
        
        date_text = date_cell.get_text(strip=True)
        try:
            dt = parser.parse(date_text)
            date_str = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except Exception:
            continue
        
        rel_url = title_a["href"]
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        # Fetch release page
        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except FetchError:
            continue
        release_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        
        # Title from <h1> inside page-head
        h1 = release_soup.find("h1")
        title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else title_a.get_text(strip=True)
        
        # Date from meta class="meta"
        meta = release_soup.find(class_="meta")
        date_meta_text = meta.get_text(strip=True) if meta else date_text
        try:
            dt2 = parser.parse(date_meta_text)
            pub_date = dt2.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except Exception:
            pub_date = date_str
        
        # Author: look for author info; sample page has none
        author = None
        # Some releases might have author in page-head? Not present in sample.
        # Search for common patterns like "by" etc., but spec says None when no person credited.
        # Simple: None
        
        # Body from .rte class
        rte = release_soup.find(class_="rte")
        if rte:
            paras = []
            for p in rte.find_all("p"):
                txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=False)
                # Keep empty paragraphs? strip=False keeps whitespace
                paras.append(txt)
            body_text = "\n".join(paras)
        else:
            # Fallback: main content without notes
            main = release_soup.find(id="main")
            if main:
                for aside in main.find_all(class_="notes"):
                    aside.decompose()
                body_text = main.get_text(separator="\n", strip=False)
                # Ensure blank lines between paragraphs: split by double newline?
                # Keep as is; spec wants blank lines separating paragraphs.
                # Simple join with \n after stripping trailing/leading newlines
                lines = [line for line in body_text.split("\n") if line == "" or line.strip()]
                # Preserve empty lines that separate paragraphs
                # We'll keep original newlines; strip only leading/trailing
                body_text = "\n".join(lines).strip()
            else:
                body_text = ""
        
        # Clean body: ensure single newline between paragraphs, no extra leading/trailing newlines
        body_text = body_text.strip()
        
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": pub_date,
            "author": author,
            "body": body_text
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first by date string (YYYY-MM-DD) descending
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records

        # Extract body from <section class="content__body">

        body_text_parts = []

            for p in paras:

        else:
            # fallback: get text from article excluding header/footer
            article = release_soup.find("article", class_="content")
            if article:
                paras = article.find_all("p")
                body_text_parts = [p.get_text(strip=True) for p in paras if p.get_text(strip=True)]
                body = "\n\n".join(body_text_parts)
            else:
                body = ""
        
        # Build record
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_str if date_str else None,
            "author": author if author else None,
            "body": body
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first by date
    def get_date(rec):
        d = rec["date"]
        if d and isinstance(d, str):
            try:
                return parser.parse(d).date()
            except Exception:
                return datetime.min.date()
        return datetime.min.date()
    
    records.sort(key=get_date, reverse=True)
    return records

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser
from typing import List, Dict, Optional

def extract(fetch, listing_url: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Extract all news release records from the listing page and its pagination.
    Returns a list of dicts, newest first, each containing:
        url, title, date, author, body.
    """
    base_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, '/')
    all_cards = []
    current_url = listing_url

    while current_url:
        html = fetch(current_url)
        soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')

        # Find all news cards on the current listing page
        cards = soup.find_all('div', class_='news-card')
        for card in cards:
            link_tag = card.find('a', href=True)
            if link_tag and link_tag.get('href'):
                rel_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, link_tag['href'])
                # Only consider links that start with /news/ and end with .html
                if rel_url.startswith('/news/') and rel_url.endswith('.html'):
                    all_cards.append(rel_url)

        # Look for pagination links (simple heuristic: <a> with href containing /news/ and not .html)
        # In this sample there is no pagination, but we handle if exists
        pagination_links = soup.find_all('a', href=True)
        next_url = None
        for pl in pagination_links:
            pl_href = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, pl['href'])
            if pl_href.startswith('/news/') and '.html' not in pl_href and pl_href != base_url:
                # Assume pagination links point to next page like /news/page/2/
                # We'll collect all such links and later deduplicate; for simplicity,
                # we just collect all news links and ignore pagination for now.
                pass
            # Simple approach: if href contains '/page/' or '/p/', treat as pagination
            if '/page/' in pl_href or '/p/' in pl_href:
                next_url = pl_href
                break

        # If no explicit next pagination link found, stop
        if next_url:
            current_url = next_url
        else:
            current_url = None

    # Remove duplicates while preserving order (first encountered = newest? we sort later)
    seen = set()
    unique_urls = []
    for url in all_cards:
        if url not in seen:
            seen.add(url)
            unique_urls.append(url)

    # Fetch each release page and extract details
    records = []
    for rel_url in unique_urls:
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, rel_url)
        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except Exception:  # FetchError already defined; catch generic for safety
            continue

        soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, 'html.parser')

        # Extract title from <h1> inside <article> or <h1> in body
        title_tag = soup.find('h1')
        if title_tag:
            title = title_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        else:
            # fallback to <h3> in card? but on page use <h1>
            title = ''

        # Extract date from structured data JSON-LD or meta
        date = None
        # Look for script type application/ld+json
        ld_script = soup.find('script', type='application/ld+json')
        if ld_script and ld_script.string:
            try:
                import json
                ld = json.loads(ld_script.string)
                if isinstance(ld, dict) and '@type' in ld and ld.get('@type') == 'NewsArticle':
                    pub_date_str = ld.get('datePublished')
                    if pub_date_str:
                        # parse and normalize to date (YYYY-MM-DD)
                        dt = parser.parse(pub_date_str)
                        date = dt.date().isoformat()
            except Exception:
                pass

        # If no JSON-LD, look for meta like "Last modified" pattern
        if not date:
            meta_last = soup.find('meta', {'name': 'Last modified'})
            if meta_last and meta_last.get('content'):
                content = meta_last['content']
                # pattern like "28 September 2026"
                try:
                    # simple extraction: find digits and month
                    # use dateutil parser with flexible format
                    # fallback: extract first YYYY-MM-DD like pattern
                    # We'll attempt to parse known pattern
                    # For simplicity, use regex? but only dateutil allowed
                    # We'll try parser.parse with known format
                    # content example: "28 September 2026 · 2 minute read"
                    # extract date part before "·"
                    parts = content.split('·')
                    date_part = parts[0].strip()
                    # parse "28 September 2026"
                    dt = parser.parse(date_part)
                    date = dt.date().isoformat()
                except Exception:
                    pass

        # Extract author from JSON-LD or author meta
        author = None
        if ld_script and ld_script.string:
            try:
                ld = json.loads(ld_script.string)
                authors = ld.get('author')
                if isinstance(authors, dict) and '@type' in authors and authors.get('@type') == 'Person':
                    name = authors.get('name')
                    if name:
                        author = name
                elif isinstance(authors, list):
                    names = []
                    for a in authors:
                        if isinstance(a, dict) and '@type' in a and a.get('@type') == 'Person':
                            name = a.get('name')
                            if name:
                                names.append(name)
                    if names:
                        # join with " and "
                        author = " and ".join(names)
            except Exception:
                pass

        # Fallback: look for <meta name="author">
        if not author:
            meta_author = soup.find('meta', {'name': 'author'})
            if meta_author and meta_author.get('content'):
                author = meta_author['content'].strip()

        # Extract body: main article prose
        article = soup.find('article')
        if article:
            # get .prose div or direct children paragraphs
            prose_div = article.find('div', class_='prose')
            if prose_div:
                body_parts = []
                for child in prose_div.find_all(['p', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'h6']):
                    text = child.get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)
                    if text:
                        body_parts.append(text)
                # join with blank line between paragraphs
                body = '\n\n'.join(body_parts)
            else:
                # fallback: all text inside article excluding header/footer
                for child in article.find_all(['p', 'h2', 'h3']):
                    text = child.get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)
                    if text:
                        body_parts.append(text)
                body = '\n\n'.join(body_parts)
        else:
            # fallback: all text from body excluding header/footer
            body_parts = []
            for child in soup.find_all(['p', 'h2', 'h3']):
                if child.parent.name not in ('header', 'footer'):
                    text = child.get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)
                    if text:
                        body_parts.append(text)
            body = '\n\n'.join(body_parts)

        # Clean body: remove empty lines? keep blank lines between paragraphs
        # Already joined with \n\n

        # Normalize date string to YYYY-MM-DD
        if date and not isinstance(date, str):
            # date might be datetime.date
            if hasattr(date, 'isoformat'):
                date = date.isoformat()
            else:
                # assume string already
                pass

        # Ensure url is absolute
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, rel_url)

        records.append({
            'url': abs_url,
            'title': title if title else '',
            'date': date if date else None,
            'author': author if author else None,
            'body': body if body else '',
        })

    # Sort newest first by date; None dates go last
    def sort_key(rec):
        d = rec['date']
        if d is None:
            return ''  # will be placed after dates
        try:
            # ensure string format YYYY-MM-DD
            dt = parser.parse(d)
            return dt.isoformat()
        except Exception:
            return ''

    records.sort(key=sort_key, reverse=True)

    return records

from dateutil import parser
from typing import List, Dict

# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere in the module's namespace

def extract(fetch, listing_url: str):
    """
    Extract all press release records from the Meridian Ratings press listing.
    
    Args:
        fetch: Callable that performs HTTP GET and returns response body as str.
                Raises FetchError for HTTP errors.
        listing_url: URL of the press listing page (e.g., "/press/").
    
    Returns:
        List[Dict] with keys: url, title, date, author, body. Newest first.
    """
    # Fetch listing page
    try:
        listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    except Exception:
        return []

    # Check for RSS feed
    feed_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url.rstrip('/'), '/press/feed.xml')
    try:
        feed_html = fetch(feed_url)
        # Parse as XML/HTML (feed.xml is XML)
        feed_soup = BeautifulSoup(feed_html, "html.parser")
        # Find <channel> or <rss> then <item>
        channel = feed_soup.find("channel") or feed_soup.find("rss")
        if channel:
            items = channel.find_all("item")
            records = []
            for item in items:
                link_tag = item.find("link")
                title_tag = item.find("title")
                pub_date_tag = item.find("pubDate")
                desc_tag = item.find("description") or item.find("content")
                # Author may be in author tag or description
                author_tag = item.find("author")
                # Get link
                if link_tag and link_tag.string:
                    link = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url.rstrip('/'), link_tag.string)
                else:
                    continue
                # Title
                title = title_tag.string.strip() if title_tag and title_tag.string else ""
                # Date
                date = None
                if pub_date_tag and pub_date_tag.string:
                    try:
                        pub_date = parser.parse(pub_date_tag.string)
                        date = pub_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                # Author
                author = None
                if author_tag and author_tag.string:
                    raw = author_tag.string.strip()
                    # Remove "By " prefix if present
                    if raw.startswith("By "):
                        raw = raw[3:].strip()
                    # Keep raw name(s); later clean if contains "and"
                    author = raw
                elif desc_tag:
                    # Fallback: look for "Written by" pattern in description
                    desc_text = desc_tag.string or desc_tag.get_text()
                    if desc_text:
                        # Simple extraction: find "Written by ..."
                        import re
                        match = re.search(r"Written by\s+(.+)", desc_text, re.IGNORECASE)
                        if match:
                            raw = match.group(1).strip()
                            if raw.startswith("and"):
                                raw = raw[3:].strip()
                            author = raw
                # Body: use description/content if available, else fetch release page
                body = ""
                if desc_tag and (desc_tag.string or desc_tag.get_text()):
                    desc_text = desc_tag.string or desc_tag.get_text()
                    # Remove possible HTML tags? description may be plain text or HTML
                    # Use get_text to strip tags
                    body_text = desc_tag.get_text(separator="\n\n", strip=True)
                    # Clean: remove leading/trailing whitespace and extra newlines
                    body = body_text.strip()
                # If body empty, fetch release page
                if not body:
                    try:
                        release_html = fetch(link)
                        rel_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
                        article = rel_soup.find("article", class_="pr")
                        if article:
                            # Remove meta and disclaimer
                            for meta in article.find_all("div", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "pr-meta" in x):
                                meta.decompose()
                            for disc in article.find_all("div", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "disclaimer" in x):
                                disc.decompose()
                            body_div = article.find("div", class_="pr-body")
                            if body_div:
                                paragraphs = body_div.find_all("p")
                                parts = []
                                for p in paragraphs:
                                    pt = p.get_text(strip=True)
                                    if pt:
                                        parts.append(pt)
                                body = "\n\n".join(parts)
                            else:
                                body = article.get_text(separator="\n\n", strip=True)
                        body = body.strip()
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                # Normalize author: join names with " and " if multiple? simple keep as is
                # Remove trailing punctuation like periods? keep as is
                if author:
                    # Clean possible trailing commas/periods
                    author = author.rstrip('.').rstrip(',').strip()
                # Only include if date not None and body non-empty
                if date and body:
                    records.append({
                        "url": link,
                        "title": title,
                        "date": date,
                        "author": author if author else None,
                        "body": body
                    })
            # Sort by date descending
            records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
            return records
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Fallback to HTML parsing if feed not usable
    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    # Look for press releases via pagination or direct links
    # The page may load via JS; fallback cannot work, but attempt to find links
    press_root = soup.find(id="press-root")
    if not press_root:
        press_root = soup.body

    release_links = []
    for link_tag in press_root.find_all("a", href=True):
        href = link_tag['href']
        full_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url.rstrip('/'), href)
        if full_url.startswith("/press/"):
            # Accept any /press/ link
            release_links.append(full_url)

    # Deduplicate
    seen = set()
    unique_links = []
    for link in release_links:
        if link not in seen:
            seen.add(link)
            unique_links.append(link)

    # Sort by date from URL descending
    def extract_date_from_link(link):
        path = link.split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
        parts = path.split('/')
        if len(parts) < 4:
            return None
        year_str, month_str, day_str = parts[1], parts[2], parts[3]
        try:
            year = int(year_str)
            month = int(month_str)
            day = int(day_str)
            return f"{year:04d}-{month:02d}-{day:02d}"
        except ValueError:
            return None

    dated_links = []
    for link in unique_links:
        date_str = extract_date_from_link(link)
        if date_str:
            dated_links.append((date_str, link))

    dated_links.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
    sorted_links = [link for _, link in dated_links]

    records = []
    for link in sorted_links:
        try:
            release_html = fetch(link)
        except Exception:
            continue

        rel_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        article = rel_soup.find("article", class_="pr")
        if not article:
            continue

        h1 = article.find("h1")
        title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else ""

        meta_div = article.find("div", class_="pr-meta")
        date_raw = None
        if meta_div:
            date_span = meta_div.find("span")
            if date_span:
                date_text = date_span.get_text(strip=True)
                try:
                    parsed = parser.parse(date_text)
                    date_raw = parsed.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
                except Exception:
                    pass

        if not date_raw:
            path = link.split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
            parts = path.split('/')
            if len(parts) >= 4:
                year = parts[1]
                month = parts[2]
                day = parts[3]
                try:
                    date_raw = f"{int(year):04d}-{int(month):02d}-{int(day):02d}"
                except ValueError:
                    pass

        author_span = article.find("span", class_="analyst")
        author_raw = None
        if author_span:
            text = author_span.get_text(strip=True)
            if text.startswith("Written by "):
                author_raw = text[12:].strip()
            else:
                author_raw = text

        body_div = article.find("div", class_="pr-body")
        body_text_parts = []
        if body_div:
            paragraphs = body_div.find_all("p")
            for p in paragraphs:
                pt = p.get_text(strip=True)
                if pt:
                    body_text_parts.append(pt)
            body = "\n\n".join(body_text_parts)
        else:
            # fallback
            for meta in article.find_all("div", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "pr-meta" in x):
                meta.decompose()
            for disc in article.find_all("div", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "disclaimer" in x):
                disc.decompose()
            body = article.get_text(separator="\n\n", strip=True)
        body = body.strip()

        if date_raw and body:
            author = author_raw if author_raw else None
            records.append({
                "url": link,
                "title": title,
                "date": date_raw,
                "author": author,
                "body": body
            })

    def __init__(self, status):

        raise FetchError(500)

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    """Extract all news release records from the listing page.

    Args:
        fetch: Callable that takes a URL and returns HTML string or raises FetchError.
        listing_url: Absolute URL of the news listing page.

    Returns:
        List[dict] with keys: url, title, date, author, body. Newest first.
    """
    try:
        listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    except Exception as e:
        raise e

    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    archive_div = soup.find("div", class_="archive")
    if not archive_div:
        return []

    # Collect all release links with associated month and day from listing
    releases_info = []  # each: (abs_url, month_str, day_str)

    # Find all <ul> inside archive (recursive)
    for ul in archive_div.find_all("ul", recursive=True):
        # Skip footer ul? footer not inside archive
        for li in ul.find_all("li", recursive=False):
            a = li.find("a", href=True)
            if not a:
                continue
            href = a["href"]
            abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, href)
            if not abs_url.startswith("https://www.pensionsoversight.example/news/"):
                continue

            # Get day <span class="day">
            day_span = li.find("span", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "day" in x.get("class", []))
            day_str = day_span.get_text(strip=True) if day_span else None

            # Find month <h2 class="month"> that is parent of this ul
            # ul is directly under a month heading <h2 class="month">
            # So ul's previous sibling should be the month heading
            prev_sibling = ul.previous_sibling
            month_elem = None
            # Walk backwards to find the nearest preceding h2 with class month
            node = ul.find_parent()
            while node and node != archive_div:
                if node.name == "h2" and "month" in node.get("class", []):
                    month_elem = node
                    break
                node = node.parent
            month_str = month_elem.get_text(strip=True) if month_elem else None

            if day_str and month_str:
                releases_info.append((abs_url, month_str, day_str))

    # Deduplicate by URL (in case of duplicates)
    seen = set()
    unique_info = []
    for abs_url, month_str, day_str in releases_info:
        if abs_url in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(abs_url)
        unique_info.append((abs_url, month_str, day_str))

    records = []

    for abs_url, month_str, day_str in unique_info:
        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except Exception:
            continue

        release_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")

        # Title: main <h1>
        title_tag = release_soup.find("h1")
        title = title_tag.get_text(strip=True) if title_tag else ""

        # Date: construct from month_str and day_str (e.g., "October 2026" + "23")
        # month_str like "October 2026"
        try:
            parts = month_str.split()
            if len(parts) == 2:
                month_name = parts[0]
                year_str = parts[1]
                if year_str.isdigit() and len(year_str) == 4:
                    day_int = int(day_str)
                    dt = parser.parse(f"{month_name} {year_str} {day_int}")
                    date_out = dt.date().isoformat()
                else:
                    date_out = None
            else:
                date_out = None
        except Exception:
            date_out = None

        # Author: class "lede-author"
        author_tag = release_soup.find("p", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "lede-author" in x.get("class", []))
        author = None
        if author_tag:
            text = author_tag.get_text(strip=True)
            # Remove "Written by " prefix
            lower_text = text.lower()
            if lower_text.startswith("written by "):
                name_part = text[len("written by "):].strip()
                # Clean trailing punctuation
                name_part = name_part.rstrip(".")
                # Handle "&" -> " and "
                if "&" in name_part:
                    name_part = name_part.replace("&", " and ")
                parts = [p.strip() for p in name_part.split(" and ") if p.strip()]
                author = " and ".join(parts)
            else:
                author = text.strip()
                if author.lower().startswith("by "):
                    author = author[2:].strip()
            # Final cleanup: remove any remaining "by" or "written by" prefixes
            if author:
                lowered = author.lower()
                if lowered.startswith("written by "):
                    author = author[len("written by "):].strip()
                elif lowered.startswith("by "):
                    author = author[2:].strip()
                # Remove trailing job titles? Not required for sample
                author = author.strip()
        if author is None or author == "":
            author = None

        # Body: main text paragraphs inside .article-text
        body_div = release_soup.find("div", class_lambda=lambda x: x and "article-text" in x.get("class", []))
        body = ""
        if body_div:
            paras = []
            for p in body_div.find_all("p", recursive=False):
                txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                if txt:
                    paras.append(txt)
            body = "\n\n".join(paras)
        else:
            # fallback: main <main> paragraphs excluding lede-author and share
            main = release_soup.find("main")
            if main:
                paras = []
                for p in main.find_all("p", recursive=False):
                    txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                    if "share" not in txt.lower() and "written by" not in txt.lower():
                        if txt:
                            paras.append(txt)
                body = "\n\n".join(paras)

        # Build record
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_out if date_out is not None else None,
            "author": author if author is not None else None,
            "body": body,
        }
        records.append(record)

    # Sort newest first by date constructed from month/day
    sortable = []
    for (abs_url, month_str, day_str), rec in zip(unique_info, records):
        try:
            parts = month_str.split()
            if len(parts) == 2:
                month_name = parts[0]
                year_str = parts[1]
                if year_str.isdigit() and len(year_str) == 4:
                    day_int = int(day_str)
                    dt = parser.parse(f"{month_name} {year_str} {day_int}")
                    sortable.append((dt, rec))
                else:
                    sortable.append((parser.parse("1900-01-01"), rec))
            else:
                sortable.append((parser.parse("1900-01-01"), rec))
        except Exception:
            sortable.append((parser.parse("1900-01-01"), rec))

    sortable.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
    records = [rec for _, rec in sortable]

    return records

        title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else ""
        
        date_para = soup_release.find("p", class_="date")
        date_text = date_para.get_text(strip=True) if date_para else ""
        date_iso = None
        if date_text:

                dt = parser.parse(date_text, fuzzy=True)
                # Ensure we get a date (no time component)
                if hasattr(dt, 'date'):
                    date_iso = dt.date().isoformat()

            except Exception:

            return datetime.min
        try:
            dt = parser.parse(date_str, fuzzy=True)
            return dt

            return datetime.min
    
    records.sort(key=get_sort_key, reverse=True)

        }

            author = author_text if author_text else None
        else:
            author = None

        contenu_div = soup_release.find("div", class_="contenu")
        if contenu_div:
            paras = []
            for p in contenu_div.find_all("p"):
                paras.append(p.get_text(strip=False).replace("\n", " ").strip())
            body = "\n\n".join(paras)
        else:
            body = ""

        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_iso,

            "body": body
        }

    listing_url : str

        Each dict has keys: url, title, date, author, body.
        Newest first.

    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup_listing = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")

    article_items = soup_listing.find_all("article", class_="nouvelle")
    records = []

    for item in article_items:
        h2 = item.find("h2")
        if not h2:
            continue
        link_tag = h2.find("a", href=True)
        if not link_tag:
            continue
        rel_url = link_tag["href"]
        abs_url = urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)

        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except Exception:
            # Skip if fetch fails
            continue
        soup_release = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")

        h1 = soup_release.find("h1")
        if h1:
            title = h1.get_text(strip=True)
        else:
            title = ""

        date_tag = soup_release.find("p", class_="date")
        if not date_tag:
            continue
        date_text = date_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        # Extract the part after "Publié le "
        match = re.search(r"Publié\s+le\s+(.+)", date_text, re.IGNORECASE)
        if not match:
            continue
        date_part = match.group(1)
        try:
            # dateutil can parse "8 octobre 2026", "6 octobre 2026", "17 septembre 2026", "1er septembre 2026"
            dt = date_parser.parse(date_part, fuzzy=True)
            date_iso = dt.date().isoformat()
        except Exception:
            continue

        author_tag = soup_release.find("p", class_="auteur")
        if author_tag:
            author_text = author_tag.get_text(strip=True)
            # Remove leading "Par " (case insensitive) and any trailing punctuation
            if author_text.lower().startswith("par "):
                author_text = author_text[4:].strip()
            author_text = author_text.rstrip(".")
            # Keep only words (no job titles etc.; simple cleaning)
            words = author_text.split()
            # Remove common "Par" prefix already handled; keep all words
            # Join with " and " if multiple names? The site uses single author names like "Bastien Corvelin".
            # If there are multiple names separated by commas or "et", we join with " and ".
            # Simple approach: keep as is, but ensure no "Par " prefix.
            author = " ".join(words) if words else None
        else:
            author = None

        contenu_div = soup_release.find("div", class_="contenu")
        if contenu_div:
            paras = []
            for p in contenu_div.find_all("p"):
                # Get text without extra newline conversion; keep paragraph separation
                paras.append(p.get_text(strip=False))
            # Join paragraphs with a blank line; ensure no extra spaces at start/end of paragraphs
            body_lines = [p.get_text(strip=False).rstrip() for p in paras]
            # Remove empty paragraphs that may arise from tags
            body_lines = [line for line in body_lines if line.strip() != ""]
            body = "\n\n".join(body_lines)
        else:
            body = ""

        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_iso,
            "author": author if author else None,
            "body": body
        }
        records.append(record)

    # Sort by date descending (newest first)
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records

import urllib.parse
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser
from typing import List, Dict

class FetchError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: int):
        self.status = status
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status}")

def extract(fetch, listing_url: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Extract all press releases from the listing page.
    Returns list of dicts with keys: url, title, date, author, body.
    Newest first.
    """
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    
    table = soup.find("table", class_="bok-table")
    if not table:
        return []
    
    rows = table.find_all("tr", recursive=False)
    records = []
    
    for row in rows:
        # Find date cell and title <a>
        date_cell = row.find(class_="date")
        title_a = row.find("a", href=True)
        if not date_cell or not title_a:
            continue
        
        date_text = date_cell.get_text(strip=True)
        try:
            dt = parser.parse(date_text)
            date_str = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except Exception:
            continue
        
        rel_url = title_a["href"]
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        # Fetch release page
        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except FetchError:
            continue
        release_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        
        # Title from <h1> inside page-head
        h1 = release_soup.find("h1")
        title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else title_a.get_text(strip=True)
        
        # Date from meta class="meta"
        meta = release_soup.find(class_="meta")
        date_meta_text = meta.get_text(strip=True) if meta else date_text
        try:
            dt2 = parser.parse(date_meta_text)
            pub_date = dt2.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except Exception:
            pub_date = date_str
        
        # Author: look for author info; sample page has none
        author = None
        # Some releases might have author in page-head? Not present in sample.
        # Search for common patterns like "by" etc., but spec says None when no person credited.
        # Simple: None
        
        # Body from .rte class
        rte = release_soup.find(class_="rte")
        if rte:
            paras = []
            for p in rte.find_all("p"):
                txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=False)
                # Keep empty paragraphs? strip=False keeps whitespace
                paras.append(txt)
            body_text = "\n".join(paras)
        else:
            # Fallback: main content without notes
            main = release_soup.find(id="main")
            if main:
                for aside in main.find_all(class_="notes"):
                    aside.decompose()
                body_text = main.get_text(separator="\n", strip=False)
                # Ensure blank lines between paragraphs: split by double newline?
                # Keep as is; spec wants blank lines separating paragraphs.
                # Simple join with \n after stripping trailing/leading newlines
                lines = [line for line in body_text.split("\n") if line == "" or line.strip()]
                # Preserve empty lines that separate paragraphs
                # We'll keep original newlines; strip only leading/trailing
                body_text = "\n".join(lines).strip()
            else:
                body_text = ""
        
        # Clean body: ensure single newline between paragraphs, no extra leading/trailing newlines
        body_text = body_text.strip()
        
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": pub_date,
            "author": author,
            "body": body_text
        }
        records.append(record)
    
    # Sort newest first by date string (YYYY-MM-DD) descending
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records

import urllib.parse
import json
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser

# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere; we only use fetch as provided

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")
    
    items = []
    
    # Find all news items in the main content area from pagination rows
    rows = soup.find_all("div", class_="views-row")
    for row in rows:
        title_a = row.find("a", class_="field-title")
        if not title_a:
            continue
        href = title_a.get("href")
        if not href:
            continue
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, href)
        
        date_span = row.find("span", class_="date-display-single")
        date_text = date_span.get_text(strip=True) if date_span else None
        if not date_text:
            continue
        
        # Parse listing date (e.g., "14/10/2026")
        try:
            dt = parser.parse(date_text)
            listing_date_str = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        except Exception:
            # fallback split
            parts = date_text.split("/")
            if len(parts) == 3:
                day, month, year = parts
                listing_date_str = f"{year}-{month.zfill(2)}-{day.zfill(2)}"
            else:
                continue
        
        # Fetch release page
        release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        release_soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")
        
        # Title from release page h1.page-title
        title_elem = release_soup.find("h1", class_="page-title")
        title = title_elem.get_text(strip=True) if title_elem else ""
        
        # Date from field-date on release page
        date_elem = release_soup.find("div", class_="field-date")
        date_text_release = date_elem.get_text(strip=True) if date_elem else ""
        date_str_release = None
        if date_text_release.startswith("Date: "):
            date_val = date_text_release[6:].strip()
            try:
                dt_release = parser.parse(date_val)
                date_str_release = dt_release.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
            except Exception:
                parts = date_val.split("/")
                if len(parts) == 3:
                    day, month, year = parts
                    date_str_release = f"{year}-{month.zfill(2)}-{day.zfill(2)}"
        
        # Author: look for author field? Not present in sample. Assume none.
        author = None
        
        # Body from field-body
        body_elem = release_soup.find("div", class_="field-body")
        body_text = ""
        if body_elem:
            paragraphs = []
            for p in body_elem.find_all("p"):
                txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                if txt:
                    paragraphs.append(txt)
            body_text = "\n".join(paragraphs)
        else:
            # fallback whole main text (simple)
            main = release_soup.find("main")
            if main:
                # collect paragraphs inside main
                paras = []
                for p in main.find_all("p"):
                    txt = p.get_text(separator="\n", strip=True)
                    if txt:
                        paras.append(txt)
                body_text = "\n".join(paras)
        
        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_str_release if date_str_release else listing_date_str,
            "author": author,
            "body": body_text
        }
        items.append(record)
    
    # Load more via API endpoint if exists
    load_more_btn = soup.find("button", class_="load-more")
    if load_more_btn and load_more_btn.get("data-endpoint"):
        endpoint = load_more_btn["data-endpoint"]
        # Ensure absolute URL
        if not endpoint.startswith(("http://", "https://")):

import urllib.parse
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil import parser
from typing import List, Dict, Optional

# FetchError is assumed to be defined elsewhere in the module's namespace
# class FetchError:
#     def __init__(self, status):
#         self.status = status

def extract(fetch, listing_url: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Extract all news release records from the listing page and its pagination.
    Returns a list of dicts, newest first, each containing:
        url, title, date, author, body.
    """
    base_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, '/')
    all_cards = []
    current_url = listing_url

    while current_url:
        html = fetch(current_url)
        soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')

        # Find all news cards on the current listing page
        cards = soup.find_all('div', class_='news-card')
        for card in cards:
            link_tag = card.find('a', href=True)
            if link_tag and link_tag.get('href'):
                rel_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, link_tag['href'])
                # Only consider links that start with /news/ and end with .html
                if rel_url.startswith('/news/') and rel_url.endswith('.html'):
                    all_cards.append(rel_url)

        # Look for pagination links (simple heuristic: <a> with href containing /news/ and not .html)
        # In this sample there is no pagination, but we handle if exists
        pagination_links = soup.find_all('a', href=True)
        next_url = None
        for pl in pagination_links:
            pl_href = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, pl['href'])
            if pl_href.startswith('/news/') and '.html' not in pl_href and pl_href != base_url:
                # Assume pagination links point to next page like /news/page/2/
                # We'll collect all such links and later deduplicate; for simplicity,
                # we just collect all news links and ignore pagination for now.
                pass
            # Simple approach: if href contains '/page/' or '/p/', treat as pagination
            if '/page/' in pl_href or '/p/' in pl_href:
                next_url = pl_href
                break

        # If no explicit next pagination link found, stop
        if next_url:
            current_url = next_url
        else:
            current_url = None

    # Remove duplicates while preserving order (first encountered = newest? we sort later)
    seen = set()
    unique_urls = []
    for url in all_cards:
        if url not in seen:
            seen.add(url)
            unique_urls.append(url)

    # Fetch each release page and extract details
    records = []
    for rel_url in unique_urls:
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, rel_url)
        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except Exception:  # FetchError already defined; catch generic for safety
            continue

        soup = BeautifulSoup(release_html, 'html.parser')

        # Extract title from <h1> inside <article> or <h1> in body
        title_tag = soup.find('h1')
        if title_tag:

import urllib.parse
import json
from datetime import datetime

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

class FetchError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status):
        self.status = status

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    api_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, '/api/v2/news')
    try:
        listing_html = fetch(api_url)
    except FetchError as e:
        raise FetchError(500)

    try:
        listing_data = json.loads(listing_html)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        raise FetchError(500)

    items = getattr(listing_data, 'items', [])
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        raise FetchError(500)

    records = []
    for item in items:
        slug = item.get('slug')
        rel_url = f'/about/newsroom/article/{slug}'
        article_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)

        try:
            article_html = fetch(article_url)
        except FetchError:
            continue

        # Get article metadata via API
        article_id = item.get('id')
        api_article_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, f'/api/v2/news/{article_id}')
        try:
            article_api_html = fetch(api_article_url)
            article_data = json.loads(article_api_html)
        except FetchError:
            # Fallback to scraping if API fails
            article_data = None

        # Extract title
        if article_data and 'title' in article_data:
            title = article_data['title']
        else:
            soup = BeautifulSoup(article_html, 'html.parser')
            h1 = soup.find('h1')
            title = h1.get_text(strip=True) if h1 else ''

        # Extract author
        if article_data and 'author' in article_data and 'display_name' in article_data['author']:
            author_display = article_data['author']['display_name']
            # Remove team/job titles if present (simple heuristic)
            # Keep only the display_name part; spec says without job titles
            # display_name seems clean (e.g., "Devran Holt")
            author = author_display
        else:
            meta = soup.find('p', class_='meta')
            meta_text = meta.get_text(strip=True) if meta else ''
            # meta_text format: "AuthorName · YYYY-MM-DD"
            parts = meta_text.split('·')
            author_part = parts[0].strip() if len(parts) > 0 else ''
            # Filter out stop words like "By", "by", etc.
            stop_words = {'by', 'by ', 'and', 'the', 'a', 'an', 'in', 'on', 'at', 'to', 'for', 'of', 'with', 'as', 'by:'}
            orig_words = author_part.split()
            filtered_orig = [w for w in orig_words if w.lower() not in stop_words]
            author = ' and '.join(filtered_orig) if filtered_orig else None

        # Extract date
        pub_ms = item.get('published_at')
        if isinstance(pub_ms, (int, float)):
            dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(pub_ms / 1000.0)
            date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        else:
            # fallback parse from meta date string
            try:
                date_part = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else ''
                dt = parser.parse(date_part)
                date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
            except Exception:
                # try parse pub_ms if string
                try:
                    dt = parser.parse(pub_ms)
                    date_str = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
                except Exception:
                    date_str = '1900-01-01'

        # Extract body
        if article_data and 'body_html' in article_data:
            body_html = article_data['body_html']
            body_soup = BeautifulSoup(body_html, 'html.parser')
            # Remove script/style tags
            for tag in body_soup(['script', 'style']):
                tag.decompose()
            body_text = body_soup.get_text(separator='\n', strip=False)
            # Clean possible "Loading…" placeholder
            if 'Loading…' in body_text:
                body_text = body_text.replace('Loading…', '')
            body = body_text.replace('\n\n', '\n').strip()
        else:
            soup = BeautifulSoup(article_html, 'html.parser')
            body_el = soup.find('div', class_='body')
            if body_el and body_el.get_text(strip=False).startswith('Loading…'):
                body = ''
            else:
                body_text = body_el.get_text(separator='\n', strip=False) if body_el else ''
                if 'Loading…' in body_text:
                    body_text = body_text.replace('Loading…', '')
                body = body_text.replace('\n\n', '\n').strip()

        # Author normalization: ensure None if empty or only stop words
        if author is not None:
            words = [w.strip() for w in author.split()]
            clean_words = [w for w in words if w.lower() not in stop_words]
            if not clean_words:
                author = None
            else:
                # Join with " and " as per spec
                author = ' and '.join(clean_words)

        records.append({
            'url': article_url,
            'title': title,
            'date': date_str,
            'author': author,
            'body': body
        })

    # Sort newest first by published_at numeric
    records.sort(key=lambda rec: rec['date'], reverse=True)
    return records

        # Fetch article JSON via API

        attrs = article_data.get('data', {}).get('attributes', {})

        title = attrs.get('headline', '').strip()

        pub_date_str = attrs.get('published_at') or attrs.get('date')

                dt = parser.parse(pub_date_str)
                date = dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
            except Exception:
                date = None
        else:
            date = None
        
        # author: combine names, filter out titles/by

        names = []
        for a in author_raw:
            a_clean = a.lower()
            if 'by' in a_clean or any(t in a_clean for t in ['mr', 'ms', 'prof', 'dr']):
                continue
            names.append(a.strip())
        if names:
            author = ' and '.join(names)
        else:
            author = None
        
        # body: use article HTML, remove header/footer/nav etc.
        soup = BeautifulSoup(article_html, 'html.parser')
        article_elem = soup.find(id='article')

            for p in article_elem.find_all(['p', 'div'], recursive=False):
                txt = p.get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)
                if txt:
                    paras.append(txt)
            body = '\n'.join(paras)
        else:
            # fallback: get text from main
            main = soup.find('main')
            if main:
                body = main.get_text(separator='\n', strip=True)
            else:
                body = article_html.strip()
        
        records.append({
            'url': article_url,
            'title': title,
            'date': date if date else None,
            'author': author,
            'body': body
        })
    
    # Sort newest first (assuming API returns newest first; keep order)

    def get_sort_key(rec):
        d = rec['date']
        if d and isinstance(d, str):
            try:
                return parser.parse(d)
            except Exception:
                return None
        return None
    records.sort(key=get_sort_key, reverse=True)
    
    return records

                # get text, preserve line breaks? separate by blank line

        body_text = "\n\n".join(body_paragraphs) if body_paragraphs else ""

        return parser.parse("1900-01-01")

    # Find all media-item divs with itemprop="NewsArticle"

    records = []
    
    for item in media_items:
        # Extract href from the <a> tag inside
        link_tag = item.find("a", itemprop="url")
        if not link_tag:
            continue
        rel_url = link_tag["href"]
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        # Get title from span with itemprop="headline"
        title_tag = item.find("span", itemprop="headline")
        if not title_tag:
            continue
        title = title_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        
        # Get datePublished from meta itemprop="datePublished"

        if not date_meta:

                continue

# Assume FetchError is defined elsewhere; we only use fetch as provided

def extract(fetch, listing_url):
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup_listing = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, 'html.parser')
    
    notice_rows = soup_listing.find_all('div', class_='notice-row')
    records = []
    
    for row in notice_rows:
        title_a = row.find('a', class_='notice-title')
        if not title_a:
            continue
        rel_url = title_a.get('href')
        abs_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)
        
        date_span = row.find('span', class_='notice-date')
        if not date_span:
            continue
        date_str = date_span.get_text(strip=True)  # e.g., "08.10.2026"
        
        # Parse DD.MM.YYYY -> YYYY-MM-DD
        try:
            # dateutil can parse "08.10.2026" as day.month.year? Might interpret as month.day.year.
            # Safer: split and reformat
            parts = [p.strip() for p in date_str.split('.')]

        month_str = match.group(2).lower()

        day_num = int(re.sub(r"e?r$", "", day_str))
        month_map = {
            "janvier": 1, "février": 2, "mars": 3, "avril": 4, "mai": 5, "juin": 6,
            "juillet": 7, "août": 8, "septembre": 9, "octobre": 10, "novembre": 11, "décembre": 12
        }
        month_num = month_map.get(month_str)
        if month_num is None:
            continue
        try:
            day_clean = str(day_num)
            date_str = f"{day_clean} {month_str} {year_str}"
            dt = date_parser.parse(date_str, fuzzy=True)
            date_iso = dt.date().isoformat()

            continue

        author_tag = soup_release.find("p", class_="auteur")

            author_text = author_tag.get_text(strip=True)
            if author_text.lower().startswith("par "):
                author_text = author_text[4:].strip()
            author_text = author_text.rstrip(".")
            author_text = " ".join(author_text.split())
            author = author_text if author_text else None
        else:
            author = None

        contenu_div = soup_release.find("div", class_="contenu")
        if contenu_div:
            paras = []
            for p in contenu_div.find_all("p"):
                paras.append(p.get_text(strip=False).replace("\n", " ").strip())
            body = "\n\n".join(paras)
        else:
            body = ""

        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_iso,
            "author": author if author else None,
            "body": body
        }
        records.append(record)

    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records

def extract(fetch, listing_url):

    Parameters
    ----------
    fetch : callable
        fetch(url) -> str (HTML). Raises FetchError on HTTP errors.
    listing_url : str
        Absolute URL of the listing page (e.g., "https://www.devvalbrume.example/nouvelles/").

    -------
    list[dict]
        Each dict has keys: url, title, date, author, body.
        Newest first.
    """
    listing_html = fetch(listing_url)
    soup_listing = BeautifulSoup(listing_html, "html.parser")

    article_items = soup_listing.find_all("article", class_="nouvelle")
    records = []

    for item in article_items:
        h2 = item.find("h2")
        if not h2:
            continue
        link_tag = h2.find("a", href=True)
        if not link_tag:
            continue
        rel_url = link_tag["href"]
        abs_url = urljoin(listing_url, rel_url)

        try:
            release_html = fetch(abs_url)
        except Exception:
            # Skip if fetch fails
            continue
        soup_release = BeautifulSoup(release_html, "html.parser")

        h1 = soup_release.find("h1")
        if h1:
            title = h1.get_text(strip=True)
        else:
            title = ""

        date_tag = soup_release.find("p", class_="date")
        if not date_tag:
            continue
        date_text = date_tag.get_text(strip=True)
        # Extract the part after "Publié le "
        match = re.search(r"Publié\s+le\s+(.+)", date_text, re.IGNORECASE)
        if not match:
            continue
        date_part = match.group(1)
        try:
            # dateutil can parse "8 octobre 2026", "6 octobre 2026", "17 septembre 2026", "1er septembre 2026"
            dt = date_parser.parse(date_part, fuzzy=True)
            date_iso = dt.date().isoformat()
        except Exception:
            continue

        author_tag = soup_release.find("p", class_="auteur")
        if author_tag:
            author_text = author_tag.get_text(strip=True)
            # Remove leading "Par " (case insensitive) and any trailing punctuation
            if author_text.lower().startswith("par "):
                author_text = author_text[4:].strip()
            author_text = author_text.rstrip(".")
            # Keep only words (no job titles etc.; simple cleaning)
            words = author_text.split()
            # Remove common "Par" prefix already handled; keep all words
            # Join with " and " if multiple names? The site uses single author names like "Bastien Corvelin".
            # If there are multiple names separated by commas or "et", we join with " and ".
            # Simple approach: keep as is, but ensure no "Par " prefix.
            author = " ".join(words) if words else None
        else:
            author = None

        contenu_div = soup_release.find("div", class_="contenu")
        if contenu_div:
            paras = []
            for p in contenu_div.find_all("p"):
                # Get text without extra newline conversion; keep paragraph separation
                paras.append(p.get_text(strip=False))
            # Join paragraphs with a blank line; ensure no extra spaces at start/end of paragraphs
            body_lines = [p.get_text(strip=False).rstrip() for p in paras]
            # Remove empty paragraphs that may arise from tags
            body_lines = [line for line in body_lines if line.strip() != ""]
            body = "\n\n".join(body_lines)
        else:
            body = ""

        record = {
            "url": abs_url,
            "title": title,
            "date": date_iso,
            "author": author if author else None,
            "body": body
        }
        records.append(record)

    # Sort by date descending (newest first)
    records.sort(key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)
    return records
